description: Emergency generator 96-hour fuel supply with 10-second transfer and 30-day fuel tank inspection log required
violation_template: NCDHSR PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — EMERGENCY POWER (NC-EP-001): The construction documents for the {occupancy} project in {county} County, {city} do not demonstrate full compliance with North Carolina's emergency electrical system requirements. Specifically, the submitted drawings and specifications fail to confirm one or more of the following mandatory provisions: (1) the emergency generator fuel storage capacity must be sized for a minimum 96-hour continuous operation at full design load without resupply; (2) the automatic transfer switch (ATS) must transfer the essential electrical system to emergency power within 10 seconds of normal power loss; and (3) the construction documents must identify the location of the fuel log station and the responsible party for the required 30-day fuel tank inspection, level verification, and log entry. NFPA 110 and the FGI Guidelines as adopted by the North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services require these provisions for all licensed hospitals. Deficiencies must be corrected on the permit drawings prior to approval by the NCDHSR Construction Section.
fix_template:
1. Revise the electrical drawings and fuel system specifications to document that the emergency generator fuel tank capacity is sized for a minimum 96 continuous hours of full-load operation; provide a load calculation schedule confirming the design load figure used for sizing.
2. Confirm on the single-line electrical diagram that each automatic transfer switch (ATS) serving essential electrical system loads is rated and programmed to complete transfer within 10 seconds of normal-power failure; reference the ATS manufacturer's time-delay settings in the specifications.
3. Add a note on the mechanical or electrical site plan identifying the on-site fuel tank location, secondary containment provisions per NC DEQ requirements, and access route for resupply vehicles.
4. Include in the construction documents an operations and maintenance (O&M) note specifying the facility's obligation to maintain a written 30-day fuel-tank inspection log per NFPA 110 Section 8.3 and NCDHSR licensing requirements; indicate where the log will be stored on-site.
5. Resubmit revised drawings to the NCDHSR Construction Section, 1202 Mail Service Center, Raleigh, NC 27699-1202, for continued review.

description: Airborne Infection Isolation (AII) room required with negative pressure, minimum 12 ACH exhaust, and HEPA filtration
violation_template: NCDHSR PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — INFECTION CONTROL / VENTILATION (NC-INF-001): The mechanical construction documents submitted for the {occupancy} project in {county} County do not demonstrate that the proposed Airborne Infection Isolation (AII) room(s) comply with the ventilation requirements of 10A NCAC 14C .1917 and the FGI Guidelines as adopted by North Carolina DHSR. The following deficiencies have been identified: the AII room(s) are not confirmed to maintain a continuous negative pressure differential of at least -0.01 inches water gauge (2.5 Pa) with respect to the adjacent corridor; the minimum exhaust airflow rate of 12 air changes per hour (ACH) total, with all exhaust discharged directly to the outdoors, has not been specified; and HEPA filtration (99.97% efficiency at 0.3 microns) has not been specified at the exhaust discharge point where recirculation to another space may occur. Failure to provide code-compliant AII rooms presents a direct patient safety risk and will preclude licensure of the facility.
fix_template:
1. Revise the HVAC design to establish a minimum negative pressure differential of -0.01 inches water gauge (2.5 Pa) in each AII room relative to all adjacent spaces; provide pressure-relationship diagrams on the mechanical drawings showing all room-to-room pressure differentials.
2. Confirm the exhaust system delivers a minimum 12 total air changes per hour in each AII room; provide an air-balance schedule on the drawings listing supply CFM, exhaust CFM, net pressure relationship, and ACH for each isolation room.
3. Specify that all AII room exhaust is discharged directly to the building exterior; locate exhaust discharge points on roof or wall elevations and confirm they are separated from any air intakes per FGI Guidelines Section 2.1-3.6.
4. Where exhaust cannot be fully dedicated to outdoor discharge, specify HEPA filtration rated at minimum 99.97% efficiency at 0.3 microns at the exhaust terminal or air-handling unit prior to any recirculation; include filter housing access and replacement provisions.
5. Resubmit revised mechanical drawings and air-balance schedule to NCDHSR Construction Section for continued review, and coordinate with the infection control officer to confirm ICRA requirements are addressed.
code_references: CDC Guidelines for Environmental Infection Control 2003

description: Operating room minimum 360 SF net area; positive pressure 20 ACH; temperature 68-75 degrees F; humidity 20-60 percent
violation_template: NCDHSR PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — SURGICAL SUITE / HVAC (NC-SU-001): Review of the architectural and mechanical construction documents for the {occupancy} project in {county} County reveals that the proposed operating room(s) do not comply with one or more of the minimum standards established under 10A NCAC 14C .1909 and the FGI Guidelines for Design and Construction of Hospitals as adopted by NCDHSR. The identified deficiencies include: (1) one or more operating rooms appear to be less than the required 360 square feet net clear floor area (excluding fixed and moveable equipment); (2) the mechanical drawings do not specify that the OR is maintained at a continuous positive pressure relative to adjacent corridors and sub-sterile areas; (3) a minimum of 20 total air changes per hour (ACH) has not been confirmed on the air-balance schedule; (4) the HVAC specifications do not confirm maintenance of a temperature range of 68°F to 75°F and a relative humidity of 20% to 60% at all times the OR is occupied. These standards are mandatory for licensure and must be addressed before NCDHSR will approve construction documents.
fix_template:
1. Verify on the architectural floor plan that each operating room provides a minimum 360 square feet of net clear floor area, measured exclusive of fixed casework, booms, columns, and other fixed obstructions; revise room size or layout as necessary and add a net-area calculation note to the drawings.
2. Revise the HVAC design to maintain a continuous positive pressure differential in each OR with respect to all adjacent spaces; update the pressure-relationship diagram to show the OR at a higher pressure than the sub-sterile corridor and the scrub sink alcove.
3. Update the air-balance schedule to confirm a minimum 20 total air changes per hour in each OR, with at least 4 ACH composed of outside air; specify laminar-flow or diffuser ceiling configuration per FGI Guidelines Section 2.1-3.6 if applicable.
4. Add mechanical specifications and control sequences confirming that the temperature control system maintains a setpoint range of 68°F to 75°F and that the humidification/dehumidification system maintains relative humidity within 20% to 60% at all times; specify monitoring with a dedicated building automation system (BAS) alarm for out-of-range conditions.
5. Resubmit revised architectural and mechanical drawings, including the updated air-balance schedule and HVAC control sequences, to the NCDHSR Construction Section for review and approval.

description: Minimum patient room area 120 SF single occupancy, 100 SF per bed semi-private; toilet within room or shared with one adjacent room only
violation_template: NCDHSR PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PATIENT ROOM / ARCHITECTURAL (NC-PR-001): The architectural construction documents submitted for the {occupancy} project in {county} County do not demonstrate compliance with 10A NCAC 14C .1908 minimum patient room area and toilet access requirements. The following deficiencies have been noted: (1) one or more single-occupancy patient rooms appear to provide less than the required 120 square feet of clear floor area, measured exclusive of toilet rooms, closets, lockers, vestibules, and fixed equipment; (2) one or more semi-private (multi-bed) rooms appear to provide less than 100 square feet of clear floor area per bed; and/or (3) the in-room toilet room or water closet serving each patient does not open directly from the patient room or from a shared toilet accessible exclusively to no more than one immediately adjacent patient room. Shared toilet arrangements that require patients to enter a public corridor to reach the toilet are not permitted. NCDHSR will not approve documents that do not meet these minimum space standards.
fix_template:
1. Add net clear floor area calculations to the architectural floor plan for every patient room; confirm single-occupancy rooms are 120 SF minimum and semi-private rooms provide 100 SF per bed, measuring from finished wall face to finished wall face and excluding toilet rooms, closets, vestibules, corridors, and fixed equipment zones.
2. Revise any non-compliant rooms by adjusting room dimensions, relocating non-essential elements outside the room, or reconfiguring the unit layout to achieve the required clear floor area; clearly dimension revised rooms on the drawings.
3. Confirm that every patient sleeping position is served by an in-room toilet room or a toilet room that is directly accessible from within the patient room and from no more than one immediately adjacent patient room; show the adjacency and interconnecting door on the floor plan.
4. Ensure each toilet room serving inpatients is accessible and meets ADA 2010 Standards for Accessible Design as adopted by North Carolina; provide dimensioned toilet room plans confirming turning radius and fixture clearances.
5. Resubmit revised architectural floor plans with area calculations and toilet adjacency notes to the NCDHSR Construction Section for review and approval.

description: NFPA 101-2021 adopted statewide; automatic sprinkler system per NFPA 13 required throughout all hospital occupancies
violation_template: NCDHSR PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — FIRE AND LIFE SAFETY (NC-FLS-001): The fire protection construction documents submitted for the {occupancy} in {county} County do not confirm full compliance with the 2021 edition of NFPA 101, Life Safety Code, as adopted in North Carolina under 10A NCAC 14C, and the North Carolina State Fire Code (NCSFC). The submitted plans do not clearly demonstrate that an automatic sprinkler system designed and installed in accordance with NFPA 13 (Standard for the Installation of Sprinkler Systems) is provided throughout the entire building, including all occupied spaces, mechanical rooms, storage areas, and interstitial spaces where required. The fire alarm system narrative and riser diagrams are also insufficient to confirm compliance with NFPA 72, National Fire Alarm and Signaling Code. All sprinkler and fire alarm systems in healthcare occupancies must be submitted to and approved by both NCDHSR and the local Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) — typically the Office of the State Fire Marshal (OSFM) — before construction begins.
fix_template:
1. Provide complete NFPA 13 sprinkler system drawings, including hydraulic calculations, riser diagram, water supply test data, and reflected ceiling plan showing all sprinkler head locations, types, and coverage areas for every space in the building.
2. Confirm on the drawings that sprinkler coverage extends to all spaces including mechanical rooms, electrical rooms, storage rooms, elevator shafts (where applicable), and any interstitial or crawl space areas per NFPA 13 and NFPA 101-2021 Chapter 18.
3. Submit fire alarm system drawings and a complete system narrative per NFPA 72; include the initiating device schedule, notification appliance layout, control panel location, and annunciator panel locations on the architectural floor plans.
4. Obtain a separate permit and plan review from the North Carolina Office of the State Fire Marshal (OSFM) for all fire protection systems; provide NCDHSR with a copy of the OSFM approval letter or permit number prior to NCDHSR final approval.
5. Resubmit coordinated fire protection, fire alarm, and architectural drawings to NCDHSR and confirm coordination with the local fire jurisdiction for inspection scheduling.

description: NCDHSR Construction Section plan review and written approval required before construction begins; submit to Raleigh office
violation_template: NCDHSR PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PLAN REVIEW / GENERAL (NC-GEN-001): This comment serves as notice that construction, renovation, or alteration of a licensed healthcare facility in North Carolina may not commence until the North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services, Division of Health Service Regulation (DHSR), Construction Section has reviewed and issued written approval of the construction documents under 10A NCAC 14C .0100. A review of the submission package for the {occupancy} project in {county} County, {city} indicates that one or more of the following required elements are incomplete or missing: (a) a completed NCDHSR Plan Submittal Form (DHSR-100); (b) a statement of program describing the proposed use, occupancy, licensed bed count, and project scope; (c) the name, license number, and seal of the licensed North Carolina architect or engineer of record; and/or (d) evidence of concurrent local building department submittal. Construction commenced prior to NCDHSR approval is a violation of 10A NCAC 14C .0100 and may result in a Notice of Violation, required demolition of non-compliant work, and delay of facility licensure.
fix_template:
1. Complete and submit a NCDHSR Plan Submittal Form (DHSR-100), available on the DHSR Construction Section website; include the facility license number, contact information for the owner's representative, and the name of the licensed North Carolina design professional of record.
2. Prepare a written Statement of Program describing the full scope of work, proposed changes to licensed bed count or occupancy type, affected departments, and phasing plan for any construction in an occupied facility; attach to the submission package.
3. Ensure that all drawings bear the original seal, signature, and license number of a licensed North Carolina architect (for architectural work) and licensed North Carolina engineers (for structural, mechanical, electrical, and plumbing work); unlicensed or out-of-state seals are not accepted without a Certificate of Authorization from the NC Board of Architecture or NCBELS.
4. Submit complete construction documents — including site plan, floor plans, reflected ceiling plans, elevations, details, specifications, and all engineering disciplines — to the NCDHSR Construction Section, 1202 Mail Service Center, Raleigh, NC 27699-1202; include three (3) paper sets or submit electronically through the DHSR ePlans portal.
5. Coordinate the NCDHSR submittal with the local building department submittal; provide NCDHSR with a copy of the local building permit application receipt, and do not begin construction until both the NCDHSR written approval and the local building permit have been issued.

description: ICRA plan required for all construction in or adjacent to an occupied healthcare facility; submit with permit application to NCDHSR
violation_template: NCDHSR PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — INFECTION CONTROL / CONSTRUCTION (NC-INF-002): The construction documents submitted for the {occupancy} renovation or addition project in {county} County do not include a completed Infection Control Risk Assessment (ICRA) as required by NCDHSR and the FGI Guidelines for Design and Construction of Hospitals (as adopted by North Carolina DHSR). For any construction activity occurring within, immediately adjacent to, or sharing an HVAC system with an occupied and licensed healthcare facility, an ICRA must be prepared by the design team in coordination with the facility's infection preventionist and submitted to NCDHSR with the permit application. The ICRA must identify the dust and airborne-contaminant risk class for each affected area, specify physical containment barriers and their locations on the floor plan, define pressure relationships between the construction zone and occupied areas, and include a written monitoring and contingency plan. Without an approved ICRA, NCDHSR cannot grant construction approval for work in or adjacent to an occupied facility.
fix_template:
1. Convene a multi-disciplinary ICRA team including the architect, contractor, facility infection preventionist, and facility engineering staff to complete a formal Infection Control Risk Assessment using the FGI Guidelines ICRA matrix; assign an ICRA risk class (Class I through IV) to each area affected by construction activity.
2. Prepare an ICRA Construction Activity Plan (CAP) that documents the construction zone boundaries, type and location of temporary containment barriers (dust walls, negative-pressure enclosures, or anterooms), and sequencing for construction phasing that minimizes patient exposure.
3. Produce an ICRA floor plan overlay — clearly keyed to the architectural floor plans submitted to NCDHSR — showing all barrier locations, entry/exit points for construction personnel, route for debris removal, and adjacent patient care areas with their sensitivity class designations.
4. Include a written ICRA monitoring protocol specifying daily pressure-differential checks at the construction zone boundary, frequency of air sampling during high-risk activities (e.g., demolition, concrete cutting), and the responsible party and escalation procedure for any ICRA breach.
5. Submit the completed ICRA documentation — including the risk-class matrix, CAP narrative, and ICRA floor plan overlay — to the NCDHSR Construction Section with the permit application package; do not begin demolition or construction activity in the occupied facility until NCDHSR has issued written approval.
code_references: CDC Guidelines for Environmental Infection Control 2003

description: Operating room requires minimum 4 ACH outside air of the 20 ACH total; no recirculation via room fan-coil or unit ventilator units permitted
violation_template: NCDHSR PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — HVAC / OPERATING ROOM VENTILATION (NC-HVAC-001): The mechanical construction documents for the {occupancy} project in {county} County do not confirm compliance with the outside-air and recirculation requirements for operating rooms under 10A NCAC 14C .1909, ASHRAE 170-2021 Table 7.1, and the FGI Guidelines as adopted by North Carolina DHSR. The air-balance schedule submitted does not confirm that each operating room receives a minimum of 4 air changes per hour (ACH) of 100% outside air as part of the required 20 total ACH. Additionally, the mechanical design appears to include room-mounted fan-coil units, unit ventilators, or recirculation units within the OR, which is expressly prohibited — all supply air to the OR must be delivered through the central air-handling unit with appropriate filtration; no local recirculation units serving the OR space are permitted. These deficiencies affect patient safety through risk of surgical site infection and must be corrected before NCDHSR will approve the mechanical documents.
fix_template:
1. Revise the air-balance schedule to document both the total ACH and the outside-air ACH for each operating room; confirm a minimum of 4 ACH outside air (100% OA, not recirculated) and 20 ACH total supply air for every OR space.
2. Verify the central air-handling unit(s) serving the OR suite have an outside-air economizer or dedicated OA damper sized to deliver at minimum 4 ACH to each OR; provide AHU schedules with outside-air CFM quantities on the mechanical drawings.
3. Remove from the OR design any room-mounted fan-coil units, unit ventilators, induction units, or other local recirculation devices; all conditioned supply air must originate from the central AHU with minimum MERV-14 supply filtration per ASHRAE 170-2021.
4. Provide a reflected ceiling plan for the OR showing supply air diffuser layout consistent with a unidirectional (laminar) or semi-laminar flow pattern over the surgical field per FGI Guidelines Section 2.2-3.4; confirm diffuser coverage, throw, and location relative to the surgical table.
5. Resubmit revised mechanical drawings — including updated AHU schedules, air-balance schedule, and OR reflected ceiling plan — to the NCDHSR Construction Section; coordinate with the infection control officer to confirm the ventilation design meets ICRA requirements for the facility.
